title: Paxos prepare and accept
hook: How do Paxos prepare and accept phases choose exactly one value?

scenes.caption: Proposers suggest values, acceptors vote, and a value is chosen once a majority accepts it.
scenes.narration: Single-decree Paxos picks one value. Proposers send numbered proposals, and a value is chosen once a majority of acceptors accept it.

elements.text: Safe with any failures; live while a majority is up.

scenes.caption: Phase 1: a promise to ignore lower-numbered proposals, plus any value already accepted.
scenes.narration: In phase one the proposer sends Prepare n. An acceptor promises to ignore lower numbers, and reports the highest proposal it already accepted.

elements.text:
on Prepare(n):
  if n > promised:
    promised = n
    reply Promise(n,
      acceptedN, acceptedV)

scenes.caption: Phase 2: the proposer must re-propose the highest accepted value reported, if any.
scenes.narration: With a majority of promises, the proposer must propose the highest-numbered accepted value reported. Only if there is none may it choose its own.

elements.text:
v = value of highest acceptedN
    among promises, else own
send Accept(n, v)

on Accept(n, v):
  if n >= promised:
    accept; reply Accepted

scenes.caption: Any two majorities overlap, so a later proposal always sees a chosen value.
scenes.narration: Any two majorities share an acceptor. A later prepare quorum must include one that accepted the chosen value, forcing re-proposal.

elements.text: Any 2 of 3 include A1 or A2, so v survives.

scenes.caption: Dueling proposers can livelock, so real systems elect a distinguished proposer.
scenes.narration: Safety never depends on timing, but liveness does. Dueling proposers can livelock, so systems elect a leader. Acceptors persist state before replying.

items: Safety holds under any message loss

takeaway: Prepare blocks stale proposals and discovers earlier accepts; accept must reuse the highest accepted value, so quorum overlap guarantees only one value is ever chosen.
